ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: 3

A patient with neuroleptic malignant syndrome has a very high creatine kinase and dark urine after sustained rigidity. Which monitoring priority addresses a major organ complication of muscle breakdown in this clinical setting?

  1. Continue clinically indicated ANC monitoring
  2. Stop the suspected causative drug and arrange urgent supportive care
  3. Review medication exposure and symptom timing
  4. Monitor renal function and manage rhabdomyolysis risk
  5. Treatment-resistant schizophrenia
Answer and explanation

Monitor renal function and manage rhabdomyolysis risk

Marked CK elevation and myoglobin release can cause acute kidney injury in severe muscle injury.

Option explanations

Monitor renal function and manage rhabdomyolysis risk: Marked CK elevation and myoglobin release can cause acute kidney injury in severe muscle injury.

Treatment-resistant schizophrenia: Clozapine has a particular role after adequate trials of other antipsychotics have failed, under specialist management. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Continue clinically indicated ANC monitoring: Removal of the US clozapine REMS did not remove the risk of severe neutropenia or the need for monitoring in prescribing guidance. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Stop the suspected causative drug and arrange urgent supportive care: Suspected NMS requires urgent assessment, withdrawal of the causative agent and supportive management; severe cases may need specialist therapies. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Review medication exposure and symptom timing: A careful history of new drugs, dose changes and withdrawal helps distinguish medication syndromes from other causes. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
